hints: Resolve all four coplanar forces along two perpendicular axes: horizontally and vertically.
Set the sum of horizontal components to zero: $F\cos\alpha = 15\cos 20^\circ - 5$.
Set the sum of vertical components to zero: $F\sin\alpha = 15\sin 20^\circ + 25$.
Divide the two equations to find $\tan\alpha$ and solve for $\alpha$, then use Pythagoras or substitution to find $F$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$F\cos\alpha + 5 = 15\cos 20^\circ$$
$$F\cos\alpha = 15\cos 20^\circ - 5 \approx 14.0954 - 5 = 9.0954\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$F\sin\alpha = 15\sin 20^\circ + 25 \approx 5.1303 + 25 = 30.1303\text{ N}$$

Find the angle $\alpha$ by dividing the vertical component by the horizontal component:
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{15\sin 20^\circ + 25}{15\cos 20^\circ - 5} = \frac{30.1303}{9.0954} \approx 3.3127$$
$$\alpha = \tan^{-1}(3.3127) \approx 73.2^\circ$$

Find the magnitude of $F$ using the Pythagorean sum of its components:
$$F = \sqrt{(15\cos 20^\circ - 5)^2 + (15\sin 20^\circ + 25)^2}$$
$$F = \sqrt{9.0954^2 + 30.1303^2} = \sqrt{82.726 + 907.835} = \sqrt{990.561} \approx 31.5\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the conditions for equilibrium of coplanar forces acting at a single point:
$$\sum F_x = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \sum F_y = 0$$
The forces acting at point $P$ have horizontal components from $F$, the $5\text{ N}$ force, and the $15\text{ N}$ force at $20^\circ$ to the horizontal.

Set up the equation for horizontal equilibrium taking rightwards as positive:
$$15\cos 20^\circ - 5 - F\cos\alpha = 0$$
Add $F\cos\alpha$ to both sides:
$$F\cos\alpha = 15\cos 20^\circ - 5$$
Calculate the numerical value:
$$F\cos\alpha = 15(0.939693) - 5 = 14.09539 - 5 = 9.09539\text{ N}$$

Set up the equation for vertical equilibrium taking upwards as positive:
$$F\sin\alpha - 25 - 15\sin 20^\circ = 0$$
Rearrange to make $F\sin\alpha$ the subject:
$$F\sin\alpha = 15\sin 20^\circ + 25$$
Calculate the numerical value:
$$F\sin\alpha = 15(0.342020) + 25 = 5.13030 + 25 = 30.13030\text{ N}$$

Divide the vertical component equation by the horizontal component equation to eliminate $F$:
$$\frac{F\sin\alpha}{F\cos\alpha} = \frac{30.13030}{9.09539}$$
$$\tan\alpha = 3.31270$$
Take the inverse tangent:
$$\alpha = \tan^{-1}(3.31270) \approx 73.208^\circ \approx 73.2^\circ$$

Determine the magnitude $F$ by squaring and adding the two components:
$$F^2 = (F\cos\alpha)^2 + (F\sin\alpha)^2$$
$$F^2 = (9.09539)^2 + (30.13030)^2$$
$$F^2 = 82.7261 + 907.8350 = 990.5611$$
Take the positive square root:
$$F = \sqrt{990.5611} \approx 31.473\text{ N} \approx 31.5\text{ N}$$
